title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
why_read: A careful empirical study comparing foundation models against task-specific models for medical imaging, with honest findings about where each approach wins.
analysis: This paper compares a pretrained vision foundation model (DINOv2) against traditional from-scratch segmentation networks like U-Net on three different medical imaging tasks. It finds the foundation model generalizes better to new hospitals and scanners, but the task-specific models still edge it out on precise boundary detection when there's enough training data. It also uncovers that a commonly used benchmark dataset has duplicate images across splits, which is a genuinely useful finding for anyone using that benchmark. This kind of rigorous, nuanced comparison is valuable because most foundation-model papers oversell generalization without external validation.
